resources.string: "Explore the new terminal tools"

"## Start here

This manual is bundled with Launcher and can be read offline. IRC and network services still need a connection. Read examples here; entering them at a live prompt can perform their described actions.

- IRC: open `irc`, connect to Libera.Chat or another network, join a channel, then talk. Several networks can be connected at once. Find IRC guides in Tools.
- Calculator: use 123, ABC and FUNC, check the interpretation/result hint, and use `to` for conversions. Read Calculator help in Tools.
- Floating tools: Calculator, Help and IRC start expanded, remember their window choice and retain their floating size. Find Floating tools in Appearance.
- Termux: the separate workspace has pages and up to two independent tiles. It offers a prompted update for the APK-bundled helper. Read Termux workspace and Helper updates in Automation.
- Presets: a shared .retui package is inspected and saved first, not immediately applied. Personal .retui-backup archives are separate. Read Portable preset import in Presets.
- Startup: new installs complete the introduction, configuration and build animation before entering Launcher. Existing completed setups are kept. Read Startup setup in Getting started.
- Appearance: app-drawer category/alphabet rails have independent normal and selected colors. The default font is JetBrains Mono Nerd Font Regular; custom/system font controls remain available.
- Idle fade: optionally fade Home and the Termux workspace to the wallpaper. It is off by default. Read Idle fade in Appearance.

## Recent updates

- Build 808: colour tags show in the Settings preview and work in the time format, the edge sidebar drops cleanly, `music -info` reports your other music app, and autofill pop-ups no longer cover the command line. Build 807: Terminal mode is one pane with its own fetch and your sessions below it, Dot mode plays music with ripples and shows notification pips, shared presets can include your ASCII art, the Music widget controls your other music app when the built-in player is off, `battery_size` sizes the battery bar, and the Mono clock no longer jumps on home. Build 806: Mono on a phone held sideways shows each page in one frame, split into a left and right half, and fits beside the camera cutout. Build 805: in Terminal mode the search backdrop reaches under the navigation bar. Build 804: backups work again, Mono and Dot use both screens on foldables and the Duo, and Settings show the current mode's settings first. Build 803: switching to a moving wallpaper no longer closes the launcher, `music` commands control your other music app when the built-in player is off, and Mono panels you remove stay removed. Build 802: status formats take colour tags such as `[#FF0088]`; `home_default_module` keeps a module such as notifications open on the home; the edge sidebar has its own bezel colour, text colour and opacity; and Appearance, Behavior and the other Settings sections each have their own search box.
- eReader: `books` reads EPUB, PDF, text, Markdown and CBZ comics on e-ink paper. Select text to copy, share, translate in your own app or pin it; turn by tap, swipe or volume keys, left to right, right to left or scrolling. Read Read books with the eReader in Tools.
- Mono home: a handheld PDA of panels you arrange by holding one, on pages you swipe between or one page that scrolls, with terminal panels for your tmux windows. Read Arrange the Mono home in Appearance.
- Live TV: import M3U channels in the media player's TV tab, and watch them in Mono's media panel. Read Watch live TV channels in Tools.
- Modes: `mode` on its own suggests the other modes, and Dot mode shows how to search.
- Presets and backups: `preset -save` asks what a preset keeps, and personal backups are a full snapshot of the launcher. Read Keep personal backup separate in Presets.
- Touch Grass: a downloadable wallpaper you can part with a finger. Find it under Get more wallpapers in the wallpaper picker.
- Pixel wallpapers: shoreline (time, date or your own words with waves washing over them), dither photo, ripples and doom fire, in Settings, Personalization, Re:TUI Wallpaper.
- ASCII art: type text as ASCII art in a choice of fonts, and animate any ASCII art with effects such as decrypt, rain or glitch. Read ASCII art and effects in Appearance.
- Settings search: find any setting by name or description from the Settings hub, or with settings <words>. Read Settings search in Appearance.
- App drawer: REC, NEW and TOP tabs under the groups order the drawer by recently opened, newest installed or most used.
- Astro Chart: choose monochrome in the World list for a black sky and a planet dithered to black and white.
- Help home: use 10 from any article or topic list to return directly to the main directory.
- Notes: the library and editor share the terminal pane styling and background blur. Read Notes in Tools.
- Settings: swipe through Status, Terminal, Music, Help and Calculator previews before saving appearance changes. Read Configuration workflow in Appearance.
- Private Space: enable the private command in Behaviour on supported devices, unlock, then use `private -open <app name>`. Read Private Space in Apps.
- Calculator: basic arithmetic is ready immediately; advanced Qalculate is downloaded and installed after confirmation.

## Find an article directly

```
help -topic irc-community
```

At Launcher Home, open the offline IRC guide. `help irc` prints the shorter command reference instead. Use numbered choices or tap a topic in this reader; Android Back closes Help and keeps your place."
"IRC: connect, join and talk"

"## Open and connect

Enter `irc` at Launcher Home. The first time, Libera.Chat is selected. Tap Connect as … to join as a guest, or Sign in and enter your account name, then the masked password in the same composer. Change nickname picks the name others see.

Re:TUI's own IRC server has closed. Accounts and channels from it do not carry over; choose any public network instead.

Create account uses the same username/password flow on networks that allow signup from apps. On networks such as Libera.Chat, connect first, then use /register with your email address; the password is asked for separately and masked. Launcher never falls back to a guest connection when sign-in fails.

## Networks

The first chip under the conversation names the current network. Its marker counts unread messages and mentions on your other networks. Tap it for Networks: switch network, Add a network (Libera.Chat, OFTC, Rizon, hackint or any TLS server) or remove one. Every network stays connected while you switch.

Each network rejoins the channels you were in. Networks that were connected when you closed IRC reconnect when you open it again, when they need no password. A dropped connection retries by itself for a few minutes.

## Everyday navigation

1. Type a message in the active conversation and press ↵ to send.
2. Tap a named conversation chip to switch channels or private conversations. Unread counts and mention markers identify activity elsewhere.
3. Open Channels to switch to an open channel, browse the network, or join by name. Search text in navigation views is never posted as a message.

People lists nicknames in the active channel. Tap a nickname to open a private conversation; that alone sends nothing. Back first leaves a temporary view. From the conversation it closes the pane and disconnects every network, unless Stay connected in background is on (Networks page or /background on): then a notification keeps them connected, you show as away, and mentions and private messages notify you.

## Optional slash commands

```
/network
/network add irc.oftc.net
/join #linux
/query nickname
/help
```

Use these inside IRC, not at Launcher Home. /network lists networks and switches; Alt+← and Alt+→ also switch. /join requests membership; /query opens a private conversation without sending. Typing / offers syntax hints. Unknown slash commands are rejected, never sent as messages. `//text` sends a literal leading slash.

## Sending safely

Messages appear immediately with their confirmation state. Server echo confirms server acceptance, not recipient delivery or a read receipt. Disconnect can leave a send uncertain; it is never automatically retried. Opening this offline article does not connect, join or send anything."
"IRC accounts, reconnect and privacy"

"## Remember this device

Remember this device asks the network's NickServ to trust a protected Android Keystore key after you sign in. Create account turns it on by default; you can turn it off. Passwords are not saved. Afterwards the network reconnects without a password and rejoins your channels. It works on networks whose services accept certificates, such as Libera.Chat and OFTC.

This is a device key, not a portable restore code. A new phone, reinstall, deleted app data or a missing key needs password sign-in again. Anyone using your unlocked Launcher can use the remembered account. Keep your account password recoverable independently.

## If reconnect fails

Check your network and the server, then use Reconnect or password Sign in. A rejected key or TLS failure never silently downgrades to a guest connection. Account names belong to one network; an account on one network is not an account on another.

## Forget this device

Connection details offers Forget this device. It deletes the key from this phone. The network may still list the certificate, but nothing can use it; remove it with NickServ CERT DEL from a signed-in client if you want. Removing a network also deletes its key. Neither deletes your account.

## Privacy and retention

TLS verifies and encrypts the connection, but messages are not end-to-end encrypted. Server operators can read channel and private messages and see your connection address. Each network has its own rules and history retention. Launcher keeps no transcript on disk; with Stay connected on, conversations stay in memory while the background service runs, and mention notifications show the message text. Rotation retains conversations, but password entry cancels; leaving the pane disconnects unless Stay connected is on."
"Move, resize and reopen tool panes"

"Calculator, Help and IRC start expanded. The header window control switches between expanded and floating. Drag a floating header to move the pane, or its corners to resize it within the safe screen area. Expanding preserves the floating rectangle for later. Each tool remembers its own mode and floating bounds when closed and reopened.

Calculator and Help stay expanded in landscape; IRC can still float. Calculator has a minimum size to keep its input, hint and keypad usable rather than shrinking the pad into a scrolling keyboard. Larger fonts or a smaller screen can require a larger minimum pane.

The tools follow Launcher fonts, colors and generated-border settings. Header controls and bottom-corner clearance keep resize targets distinct from editing keys. Changing border appearance does not change calculation or network behavior.

Help is a separate reader. Opening it from Calculator keeps the expression, answer and transcript intact. Android Back or 0 closes Help immediately; reopening resumes its saved article and reading position. Numbered Topics/Categories choices navigate inside Help instead of requiring repeated Back presses.

These are Launcher-owned tool windows, not Android split-screen controls. Floating does not create a background service or keep IRC connected after its pane closes."
"Type text as ASCII art and animate it"

"## Type text as ASCII

Open Settings, then Personalization, ASCII Settings, Type text as ASCII. Type a word or a short line and pick a font: small, standard, slant, mini or shadow. The preview shows the art as the ASCII pane will, shrunk to fit. Save to ascii.txt replaces the art and turns the ASCII pane on; the previous ascii.txt is kept as ascii.txt.bak, so an imported drawing is never lost.

## Effects

An effect animates the ASCII art each time Home appears, then leaves it still: print, decrypt, slide, wipe, rain, waves, beams, burn, middleout, colorshift or glitch. Choose one in the sheet (tap the preview to replay it) or with ascii_effect in ASCII Settings. Effects work on any ascii.txt: typed, imported or coloured. Art with its own ::frame animation keeps that animation instead.

- ascii_effect_speed plays the effect slow, normal or fast.
- ascii_effect_loop_seconds plays it again after resting that many seconds; 0 plays it once each time Home appears.
- Tap the ASCII art on Home to replay the effect.

Looping pauses when Home is hidden and after two minutes without a touch, so it never runs unattended. Very large art (over 4,000 characters) stays still.

## Check the settings

```
config -get ascii_effect
config -get ascii_effect_speed
```

These only show the current values. To change them, use ASCII Settings or an explicit config -set."
"Search every setting at once"

"## Find any setting

The Settings hub has a search box above its categories. Type a few words, such as clock format, ascii loop or city: every setting on every page is searched by its name and its description, along with hub pages such as Fonts, Presets and Backup. Every word must match somewhere; hits in the name rank first.

Each result shows the setting, where it lives (for example Behavior › behavior.xml › Formats) and the first line of its description. Tap one to open that page showing just that setting. Clear the page's search box to see the whole page again. Back clears the hub search before it closes Settings.

## From the command line

```
settings clock format
```

At Launcher Home this opens Settings with that search already filled in. settings on its own opens the hub as before."
"Optional idle fade to your wallpaper"

"Idle fade is off by default. Enable breath_out in Settings and choose breath_out_seconds; its default timeout is 900 seconds (15 minutes). It fades Launcher Home and the dedicated Termux workspace to the wallpaper after inactivity. Calculator, Help and IRC are not additional fade targets.

The first touch, key or Back wakes a faded surface without performing the underlying action. Interact again to use that control. Typing restarts the timer. Backgrounding or loss of focus pauses active timing, and touch exploration prevents the fade. Disabling the feature restores the surface immediately.

This is visual fading, not screen locking, a security boundary, a phone-sleep command or a way to stop tmux jobs.

## Check the setting

```
config -get breath_out
config -get breath_out_seconds
```

These commands at Launcher Home only inspect the current values. To change them, use Settings or an explicit config -set. The two settings can be included in shareable presets."
"Update the Termux helper from the workspace"

"## Approve the matching helper

Opening the Termux workspace checks compatibility with the helper bundled in this APK. Update now installs that matching helper through Termux and reconnects the bridge. Later installs nothing. Inside the workspace, :update reopens the prompt. There is no silent update or background download from a changing Git branch.

The update replaces the normal helper path, including a custom helper there, only after approval. It verifies decoded bytes with SHA-256 and atomically replaces the file. Installation failures attempt rollback; the previous helper is retained at $PREFIX/share/retui/retui.previous. Existing shells, running jobs and workspace layout are kept. Only bridge connections restart.

## Setup is separate

Termux must already be installed, Launcher must have command permission, and allow-external-apps must be enabled in Termux by the user. If tmux or socat is missing, install them in Termux with pkg install tmux socat. The prompt offers permission, Termux and setup-guide actions; it does not silently grant access or install dependencies.

## If an update fails

Check the displayed error and prerequisites before retrying. A command with no reply may still finish inside Termux; Launcher does not automatically replay the installation. Leaving Launcher does not cancel a command already dispatched to Termux.

A lock prevents concurrent replacements. After an interrupted update, retry may report a running or interrupted lock. Launcher never deletes unknown locks automatically. Open the setup guide, inspect $PREFIX/share/retui/.update-lock only after checking that no updater is running, and retain the previous helper if recovery is needed. Never kill the tmux server as a routine update fix.

## Open the guide

```
help -topic termux-helper-updates
```

At Launcher Home, read this offline guide without changing the helper. :update belongs to the workspace local-control prompt, not the Home command parser."
"Read books with the eReader"

"## Open the library

Enter `books` at Launcher Home. ADD FOLDER picks a folder of books through Android's folder picker, so Launcher needs no storage permission; OPEN FILE opens one book. SCAN looks through your folders again. The shelves ALL, EPUB, PDF, TEXT and COMIC filter by kind, and the search box filters by name or folder. The book you were reading stays at the top. Hold a book to remove it from the library; the file itself stays where it is.

The eReader opens EPUB, PDF, plain text, Markdown and CBZ comics.

## Turn pages

- Tap the left or right quarter of the page to turn back or forward. Tap the wide middle to open the menu.
- Swipe sideways to turn, when SWIPE TO TURN is on.
- The volume keys turn pages when VOLUME KEYS TURN is on. Arrow keys, Page Up, Page Down and Space work on a keyboard.
- In SCROLL direction the book is one long column. Drag or fling it; edge taps and keys move it by most of a screen.

## The footer

The bottom left shows the page. Tap the footer to cycle what the right side shows: time left in the chapter, time left in the book, pages left in the chapter, or how much you have read. Your choice is kept.

Time estimates learn how fast you read. Each forward stretch of at least a few seconds at a believable pace nudges the estimate; quick flips, jumps and time with the book closed are left out. Until it has learned, it assumes about 220 words a minute.

## Select, copy and translate

Hold a word to select it, then drag either handle to stretch the selection; it settles on whole words when you let go. The toolbar offers Copy, Share, Pin and every app on your phone that works on selected text, such as a translator or dictionary. Tap anywhere else to clear the selection. A translator only sees the words you send it.

## Pins

Pin keeps the selected lines. A pinned passage is dotted underneath, with a pin beside it in the margin when the margin has room. Select over a pinned passage and the toolbar offers Unpin instead.

The pin at the top of the menu pins the whole page you are on; it fills in when the page is pinned. PDFs and comics have no text to select, so pinned pages are how you mark them.

The PINS tab lists PINNED LINES as quotes, with their chapter and page, then PINNED PAGES. Tap one to go there; hold it to copy or remove it. SHARE ALL sends every pinned line, with where it is, to any app as plain text. Pins stay on this phone with your place in the book.

## The menu

- The top bar: LIBRARY, search in the book (text books), and the page pin.
- The slider jumps through the book.
- CONTENTS: the book's chapters and their pages; the current one is marked.
- TEXT: font (Literata, Mono or Sans), size, margins, line spacing and justification.
- PAGES: DIRECTION, either L → R, R → L or SCROLL, kept separately for text books and for PDFs and comics, so R → L can suit manga alone. Also SWIPE TO TURN and VOLUME KEYS TURN.
- E-INK: LOOK, either E-INK paper or THEME (your launcher colours, with cyberdeck frames when that is on); grey, warm, cool or night PAPER; GRAIN; REFRESH; GHOSTING.

## E-ink

GHOSTING leaves the last page faintly behind the new one, fading over the next few turns, as an e-ink screen does. REFRESH washes the screen grey and back every 6 turns or every turn, and clears the ghosts, like an e-ink panel's full refresh. Either can be off.

PDFs and comics are shown in greys on the E-INK look. Double-tap a page to zoom in, drag to look around, and double-tap again to fit. In SCROLL, comic pages run on without a gap, for webtoons.

## Carry on from Home

```
books -last
books -last comic
```

`books -last` opens the book you read last; add epub, pdf, text or comic for the last book of that kind. In Mono, the READ panel shows your book and the last one of each other kind, and Quick has a read row. In the other modes, the READ module does the same."
"Arrange the Mono home"

"## Mono

`mode mono` turns Launcher into two colours: one ink on one paper, with a pixel font and square frames. Pick the pair under Preset in Mono's settings: e-ink lite (dark ink on grey paper), e-ink dark (light ink on dark paper) or custom, which shows mono_ink_color and mono_paper_color for your own pair. Everything else follows them. Your own colours, font and borders come back when you switch to another mode, because Mono changes nothing in your settings. The CRT filter, vignette and cyberdeck frames still apply when you turn them on.

## The panels

Home is a handheld frame: a status strip with signal, time and battery, panels on a four-column grid, an output panel over the command line, and soft keys for Apps, Search, Widgets and Settings.

- scene: pixel-art weather over a skyline.
- clock: time, date, week, battery, storage and memory.
- apps: your apps as name chips, the most used first, then each app group.
- media: music, or a video or TV channel drawn in ink.
- quick: note, timer, clipboard, reminder, calc and read.
- tasks, next and alerts: notes, what is coming up, and notifications.
- read: the book you are reading and the last book of each other kind.
- term: one window of the tmux workspace. Tap it and it fills the screen above the keyboard, with the terminal keys under it; hold text there to copy it, or hold empty space to paste. Back puts the keyboard away, Back again or done puts the panel back. Add as many as you like, in three sizes.

Panels sit on pages: swipe left and right between them, away from the screen's edges. The squares above the command line show the page; hold them to add or remove a page. The command line stays put on every page. Set mono_layout_style to scroll to put every panel on one page that scrolls down instead.

Hold a panel to change its size, move it up or down the page, swap it for another or remove it; hold a terminal to change its size or window. Each panel takes the first free spot its size fits, so a tall read:2x4 can have two small panels stacked beside it. The add panel slot at the end of a page adds one. The order is kept in mono_layout, comma separated, with a | between pages; panels fill rows left to right.

```
config -set mono_layout scene,clock,apps,media,quick,tasks|term:4x4,read,term:2x2
```

Panels only run while Home is in front. The Settings soft key opens the settings that shape this home: mode, colour preset, layout, CRT filter, vignette and weather. All settings opens the full hub."
"Watch live TV channels"

"## Add channels

`media -v` opens the media player at Videos; the TV tab is beside it. Import an M3U playlist from a file or an https link. Channels are kept on this phone; the last one you watched is remembered.

Streams on plain http:// are not encrypted, so others on the network can see or change them. Launcher explains this before adding them: accept to keep them, or skip to leave them out.

## Watch

Tap a channel to play it in the video player. In Mono, the media panel plays your last channel on Home, drawn in ink. Tap it once to show its name and controls; they hide again after a few seconds. The library button opens channels, videos to carry on with, shows and music without leaving Home.

Full screen plays the channel in colour from where the panel was. Back or Home hands it back to the panel. A live channel always rejoins live; a video at a link keeps its place.

Leaving Home stops a live channel and frees the player, so nothing streams in the background; the panel offers to resume it when you come back. Streaming uses your connection and can use mobile data."
